transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, a clinical conversational agent. I conducted your follow-up check after your cataract surgery. Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. Firstly, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're eager to get back to gardening! According to our information, you can start with light exercise, such as gardening, about 1 week after surgery. Just remember to take it easy and avoid any heavy lifting or strenuous activity for a month. Does that sound okay to you? Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, that sounds good. My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should have already started using preservative-free eye drops for dryness. If you've been using them, you should continue as directed. If you're running out, you can get some more from your GP. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for that information. I'm also experiencing sensitivity to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Mild sensitivity to bright light is normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses. If it's just a bit brighter than usual, wearing sunglasses when you're outside might help. But if it's severe or accompanied by redness and pain, we'd need to check it further. Does that make sense? Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, that makes sense. Lastly, should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay. Does that sound right to you?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, that sounds right. Thank you for answering all my questions. I don't have any more questions at the moment.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It was my pleasure to help. I'm glad I could answer your questions about your cataract surgery recovery. Do you feel that all your questions have been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I feel that all my questions have been answered. Thank you for your assistance!
